info.title: AIR Platform
info.description:
The AIR estate's conversational front door.

Send a message; the platform decides what it needs, gathers it from the specialist
services, and streams back a grounded answer. It orchestrates and owns no
capability of its own — retrieval is `air-rag`'s, classification
`air-classifier`'s, read-only calls `air-tools`', mutations `air-action`'s, and
models and stores `air-infra`'s.

**Two channels, one engine.** `POST /v1/chat` serves public conversational traffic
through the customer gateway; `POST /v1/query` serves internal business queries
through the corporate one, returning schema-validated structured output. They share
the pipeline and differ only by profile — guardrails, output contract, audit sink,
quota bucket, tool allow-list. The channel comes from your API key, not from a
header.

**Mutations are proposed, never performed.** A turn that warrants a write returns a
`proposal` and changes nothing. Executing it takes a second turn carrying
`confirm.proposal_id`; prose that merely reads as agreement executes nothing.

**Streaming.** Responses are Server-Sent Events, content-negotiated: send
`Accept: text/event-stream` to stream, anything else to receive the terminal result
as one JSON body. Every pipeline stage emits as it completes, bracketed by
`turn.start` and `turn.end`. Ignore event names you do not recognise — that is what
lets token deltas arrive later without a contract change.

Errors are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`.

get.description: Process is up. Consults nothing; never fails while the process can respond.

Whether this replica can serve a turn. Gates on air-infra, which is the one dependency without which no answer can be synthesised. Other services are reported for operator visibility but do not affect readiness.

get.summary: What this deployment can do for you
get.description: Reported per principal: routes, guardrail profile, stream shapes, session and turn ceilings as they apply to the calling key's channel.

routes.title: Routes
routes.description: Routes whose backing service is configured.

guardrails.title: Guardrails
guardrails.description: Rules active for this caller's channel.

streaming.title: Streaming
streaming.description: Which stream shapes this build emits. `token_deltas` is false until air-infra grows a streaming endpoint (docs/01-hld.md §5, §9).

CapabilitiesResponse.title: CapabilitiesResponse
CapabilitiesResponse.description:
What this deployment can actually do, for the caller in front of it.

Reported per principal: a customer key and a business key see different
routes and a different guardrail profile from the same process, and a QA
result only means something next to the capabilities that produced it.

Channel.title: Channel
Channel.description:
Which gateway a turn arrived through.

This is the platform's central distinction — see docs/01-hld.md §3. It is
resolved from the authenticated principal, never from a request header: a
client that could name its own channel could select the weaker guardrail
profile, which is the whole thing the split exists to prevent.

reachable.title: Reachable
reachable.description: None when not probed — either unconfigured, or the probe is not run here.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: Operator-facing reason. Never carries a URL, key or upstream body.

DownstreamService.title: DownstreamService
DownstreamService.description:
The AIR services a turn may call.

Values match the repository names so that a metric label, a config key and a
log line all say the same word.

HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse
HealthResponse.description:
Liveness. Deliberately dependency-free.

A liveness probe that consults a downstream is a restart loop waiting to
happen: air-infra having a bad minute would make every replica of this
service look dead and get killed, which is precisely when you need them up.

ReadyResponse.title: ReadyResponse
ReadyResponse.description:
Readiness: can this replica serve a turn at all?

``ready`` tracks air-infra alone. Every other service being down is a
narrower answer, not an unservable one (docs/01-hld.md §7), so listing them
here is reporting, not gating — and conflating the two would take the
service out of rotation for a degradation it is designed to absorb.

Route.title: Route
Route.description:
What the planner may decide a turn needs.

A route is *available* only when the service behind it is reachable and
advertises the capability, so this enum is the vocabulary, not the inventory
— `/v1/capabilities` reports which of these are live right now.
